newsitem.title: USA: USG spot jet diffs firm despite strike threat - FEB 14.
newsitem.headline: USG spot jet diffs firm despite strike threat - FEB 14.

text.p: U.S. Gulf (USG) differentials firmed slightly in very quiet trade Friday despite the threat of a strike by American Airlines pilots at midnight.
American, which buys 130,000 to 140,000 barrels per day, is the nation's second largest airline and any work stoppage is likely to trigger a downturn in jet fuel differentials, traders said.
However, sellers in the USG boosted offers of 54-grade barrels to about 3.75 cents over the NYMEX by late Friday, traders said. But buyers were scarce, with no barrels reported to have changed hands.
"People aren't climbing over each other to get things done," one market player said. "There's talk, but there's no market here."
New York Harbor prompt 54-grade barrels were talked on either side of 5.50 cents over the screen, down about 0.50 cent from Thursday's level.
-- Matt Daily, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1626
